answer: Treat every agent identity as a vertex in a trust graph that must earn its edges through verifiable work. A new vertex starts cold, like an ember that must be fed: it can only transact after staking a deposit that burns if it misbehaves, and its reputation accrues slowly from completed, paid tasks. To stop an attacker from minting thousands of cheap vertices, require each one to pass a karst-like proof - a slow, resource-heavy passage through unique hardware attestation and a time-locked stake - so cloning identities costs real money and time per copy, making a Sybil swarm uneconomical.
